inventoryReview: Reviewed three generated production sources: Verification/DataPageKernel.g.cs, IndexMutationKernel.g.cs and UsageMapKernel.g.cs. They contain deterministic pinned-Dafny native primitive operations without runtime support, package references, I/O or ownership authority. Existing DataPageRows, IndexPageCodec and UsageMap supply the executing adapters; source classifications elsewhere remain unchanged. New test and benchmark sources are evidence only. The exact manifest, generated-source/caller discovery and retained failure inputs cover all five kernels. Native signed long preserves the existing page-number domain without narrowing. Public parser, tree edit, statement rollback, native compatibility and platform durability obligations remain scoped in the design and open plan.

reviews.obligations: Reviewed complete pre-mutation row-compaction admission, minimum/next-distinct boundary selection, directory/free-header rewriting and composition with modeled overlapping copy/clear. Preserve slot flags, alias policy, surviving byte intervals, secure erase and untouched pooled suffix; actual CLR bulk effects remain contracts. Reviewed maximal index prefix scanning, bounded entry capacity/progress, exact header/prefix/bookmark/child/boundary emission, finite payload composition and sentinel/free-space finalization. Pointer widths/layouts are unchanged; stable list acquisition, metadata preflight and exact key-suffix copy remain premises. Reviewed exact ordered usage-bitmap selection, packed continuation classification/payload laws, decreasing rank, tolerant invalid-member skipping and strict first-failure prefix retention. Production establishes range admission once and retains matching continuation and immutable array; list effects and reference-page cancellation/return remain contracts. The shared index-entry scan must bind a found non-sentinel boundary to the negated exhaustion statement under its original bounded-array contract. Existing recovery/replacement/descriptor/visited/frame/lifecycle boundaries remain documented in formal-verification.md and their model sources; no additional recovery or page-release authority follows.
reviews.conformance: Independent complete-page row-compaction oracles cover Jet3/Jet4/ACE slots, aliases/flags, erase policies, malformed bounds, native widths, short images and untouched bytes. Index byte vectors cover leaf/intermediate headers, compressed payloads, extreme pointers, bitmap boundaries, empty keys/full pages and refusal; existing structural/native controls retain their evidence level. Bitmap tests compare every byte pattern and signed bounds against independent expansion, strict retained prefixes, reference-page return and cancellation. Focused local checks provide development feedback; settled-main CI, target/analyzer/package/trimming/NativeAOT and hosted measurements remain required. Original-algorithm microbenchmark controls and paired existing workloads retain performance evidence without treating generated code as a timing theorem. Existing cited recovery, lifecycle, parser, native and fault-injection evidence remains applicable within its stated scope.
reviews.remainingAssumptions: Stable exclusive page/array identity, retained matching continuation, correct supplied native layouts, exact CLR bulk copy/clear, list append and stable entry acquisition remain adapter contracts. Reference reads, cancellation/pool effects, complete public parser resources, ordered trees/separators, allocator ownership and containing mutation/rollback require composition. Membership and row-space compaction grant no page-release authority. Existing I/O/hash/path/snapshot/coordinator/OS and compiler/runtime contracts remain. Physical persistence, directory durability, stale-I/O fencing and fresh native-engine gaps retain E4/F6/I15/V7 and their feature requirements. No whole-library proof, new native form or unconditional performance/durability guarantee is inferred.

reviews.obligations: Reviewed exact registration/source paths for five executable modules and the complete normal-source manifest. New page/index kernels are independent verified inputs; no assumptions, external declarations, omitted verification or new shipping dependencies are admitted. Native long joins ulong/uint/byte/int under the exact allowlist and emits CLR signed arithmetic without Dafny support. Projections retain generated bodies/self references, reject omitted runtime/model descriptors and unexpected structures. Exact-signature fixed inlining metadata is reviewed with its focused rejection controls; it changes optimization advice without changing method bodies or adding runtime support. Explicit byte-frame, bitmap, length and found-boundary witness contracts must hold in both complete-inventory and separate native-translation contexts. Mandatory verifier/auditor negative controls, deterministic translation, freshness, caller discovery, exact input hashes and failure snapshots cover every registered kernel.
reviews.conformance: Focused verify-proofs, proof-review and formal-workflow regressions cover new module packaging/provenance, wrong namespaces, runtime/descriptor rejection, five-kernel dispatch, signed-long admission/refusal, exact inlining declarations, complete failure snapshots and new callers. Fresh integrity-pinned Dafny/Z3 complete-inventory verification, clean audit, both mandatory negative controls and generated freshness are required for this settled source. Ordinary CI independently gates every selected runtime/library/analyzer/trim combination; hosted benchmarks establish their measured workloads only.
reviews.remainingAssumptions: Specification adequacy, Dafny/Z3 soundness, compiler projection, C# compiler and CLR/JIT/AOT remain trusted. Source hashes establish review freshness rather than reviewer identity, adapter refinement, actual I/O effects, native interoperability or physical durability. Sequence composition proves declared effects, while their C#/BCL implementation and complete public operation composition retain explicit obligations. Target compatibility and performance require independent builds, tests and hosted measurements.
